Medical treatment in India, reviewed by a doctor before you travel

Families in Iraq, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan, Oman, Yemen, Sudan, Ghana and Ethiopia are often told that the treatment they need is unavailable at home, or costs more than they could ever raise. Usually it is available. Usually it costs far less than they fear.

TIB HIND arranges that treatment at NABH and JCI accredited hospitals in Delhi NCR — the same procedures performed in Europe and the United States, by high-volume surgical teams, at a fraction of the cost, with little or no waiting. Send us your medical reports and Dr. Annie Varughese, a US board-certified interventional cardiologist, will identify the right hospital and the right consultant for your condition.

Send my reports for review Talk to us on WhatsApp

Free. No obligation. Your reports are read by a doctor, not a salesperson.

Disclosure

Why we tell you how we get paid

Trust should not require guesswork. So before you have to ask, here is exactly who pays TIB HIND, what it means for your bill, and what keeps our advice independent.

Who pays us

Hospitals pay TIB HIND a coordination fee when we bring them a patient. That fee comes out of the hospital's revenue, not yours.

What it means for your bill

Nothing. Your bill is the same as it would be if you walked into the hospital alone. Ask the hospital directly before you commit to anything — we would rather you did.

What keeps us independent

Dr. Varughese forms her clinical opinion before any commercial conversation happens. Hospital choice is decided on surgical volume, the consultant available, ICU capability and how far you can safely travel — never on what a hospital pays us.

Most people who send us their reports are told that India is the right choice — for the majority of conditions, it plainly is. But not everyone hears that. Some cases are better managed at home. Some are too advanced for travel to be safe. Occasionally the United States is the better option despite the cost, and Dr. Varughese will say so even though we earn nothing when she does.

That is why a doctor reads your file before a coordinator ever calls you. The answer you get is the one your reports support, not the one that suits us — and it costs you nothing either way.

Read our full disclosure on fees
Process

How it works

Five steps, and you will know where you stand at every one of them.

Photo: a patient photographing an X-ray on a phone at home
01 — Day one

Send us your reports

Photographs taken on your phone are fine. Scans, discharge summaries, lab results, imaging — whatever you already have. Send them by WhatsApp, email, or through the form on this page.

Reports in Arabic, Russian or Bengali are fine; we translate them ourselves.

Photo: Dr. Varughese reviewing a scan at her desk
02 — Within 48 hours

A doctor reads your case

Dr. Varughese reads your file personally. If your condition falls outside cardiology, she consults the relevant specialist in our network before replying.

Tell us if your case is urgent and we will move it to the front.

Photo: a printed written opinion with a cost range, redacted
03 — In the same reply

A written opinion, with costs

Not a brochure. A written note explaining what your condition requires, which hospital in Delhi NCR is right for it and why, which consultant we recommend, and an estimated cost range.

Where the estimate is uncertain — and with cancer and transplant it often is — we say so, and explain what determines the final figure.

Photo: coordinator meeting a family at Delhi airport arrivals
04 — Before you travel

We arrange everything

Visa invitation letter, appointment scheduling, airport pickup, accommodation near the hospital, an interpreter who speaks your language, and food that meets your dietary requirements.

You arrive to a plan, not a phone number.

Photo: coordinator interpreting during a hospital consultation
05 — In Delhi, and after you fly home

A coordinator stays with you

Someone from TIB HIND is with you at the hospital. They attend consultations, explain what the doctors have said in your own language, and handle the paperwork so your family can concentrate on the patient.

Once you are home, we arrange your follow-up reviews with the same consultant remotely. Treatment does not end at the airport.

Start with a free review of your reports
Treatments

What we treat

Ten areas, chosen because this is where patients from our markets most often need care that is unavailable, oversubscribed or unaffordable at home. In each one we work with consultants we know by name, at hospitals whose case volumes in that specific procedure we can show you.

Photo: cardiac catheterisation lab in a Delhi NCR hospital

Heart and cardiovascular surgery

Bypass surgery, angioplasty and stenting, valve repair and replacement, TAVI, pacemaker implantation, and paediatric surgery for congenital heart defects.

Interventional cardiology is Dr. Varughese's own field. Cardiac cases receive her direct clinical involvement throughout.

Heart treatment in India
Photo: oncology day-care unit, patient with a nurse

Cancer treatment and oncology

Surgical oncology, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and targeted therapy. We also give second opinions on cancer diagnoses made elsewhere — a common request, and one that sometimes changes the treatment plan entirely.

Cancer treatment in India
Photo: physiotherapy after knee replacement

Orthopaedics and joint replacement

Total knee and hip replacement, bilateral joint replacement, robotic-assisted procedures, revision surgery where a previous implant has failed, and ACL reconstruction.

Joint replacement in India
Photo: neurosurgical theatre or MRI suite

Neurology and neurosurgery

Brain tumour surgery, aneurysm and stroke treatment, epilepsy surgery, deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's, and paediatric neurosurgery including hydrocephalus.

Neurosurgery in India
Photo: transplant ICU corridor

Liver and kidney transplant

Living-donor liver transplant, kidney transplant, and paediatric transplant, at hospitals running high-volume programmes.

Transplant for foreign nationals is tightly regulated in India. Read the legal requirements before you make any plans.

Organ transplant in India
Photo: haematology laboratory

Bone marrow transplant

Allogeneic and autologous transplant for thalassemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, leukaemia and lymphoma — including matched sibling and haploidentical donor procedures.

Bone marrow transplant in India
Photo: spinal imaging review

Spine surgery

Spinal fusion, disc replacement, minimally invasive and endoscopic discectomy, scoliosis correction, and treatment for spinal stenosis and spinal tuberculosis.

Spine surgery in India
Photo: IVF embryology laboratory

Fertility and IVF

IVF, ICSI, IUI, fertility preservation and egg freezing, with treatment for male factor infertility, PCOS and recurrent miscarriage.

Surrogacy is not permitted for foreign nationals in India under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021, and we cannot arrange it. Sex selection is a criminal offence in India and we will not discuss it.

IVF treatment in India
Photo: pre-operative bariatric consultation

Bariatric and weight loss surgery

Gastric sleeve, gastric bypass and revision bariatric surgery, with the metabolic assessment and dietetic follow-up that decide whether the result holds.

Bariatric surgery in India
Photo: endoscopy suite

Liver disease and gastroenterology

Treatment for hepatitis B and C, cirrhosis and portal hypertension, pancreatic disease, inflammatory bowel disease, and advanced endoscopic procedures.

Liver and digestive treatment in India

Costs

What treatment actually costs

Most companies in this business will not put a number on a page. We will.

Treatment in Delhi NCR typically costs between a fifth and a third of the same procedure in Europe or the United States. Turkey and Thailand sit somewhere in between, and the gap widens as the case gets more complex.

Indicative cost of the same procedure
Europe or the United States0%
Delhi NCR, accredited hospitals0%

Indicative only — the typical range is 20 to 33 per cent of the reference cost, and the gap widens as the case gets more complex. Your figure depends on the five things below, and we put a written range in your hands within 48 hours of reading your reports.

What moves the number

Complexity

A first-time procedure costs less than a revision or a case with complications already present.

Intensive care

Days in ICU are the single largest variable in most surgical estimates.

Implant or device

Valve, stent, joint or graft — the choice can change the total substantially.

Length of stay

Hospital days, plus accommodation for whoever travels with you.

Complications

Rare, but honest estimates account for them rather than pretending otherwise.

So our cost pages do something different. Each one gives a realistic range, then explains in plain language what pushes a case towards the top of it and what keeps it near the bottom. You will be able to look at your own situation and form a reasonable expectation before you speak to anyone.

Network

Where we send patients

We work only in Delhi NCR. That is a deliberate limit — it means our coordinators know the hospitals personally, know which consultant is genuinely strong in which procedure, and can be physically present when you need them.

Map: accredited hospitals across Delhi, Gurugram, Noida and Faridabad — one metropolitan area, reachable in an afternoon

How we choose the hospital for your case

01
Case volume
How many times that team performs your specific procedure each year — not how large the hospital is.
02
The named consultant
Who will actually operate, their subspecialty, and their record in cases like yours.
03
Intensive care capability
Whether the unit can hold your case if it goes badly. This decides outcomes more often than the surgery does.
04
Accreditation, verified and current
NABH or JCI, checked rather than assumed.
05
How soon you can be seen
The best surgeon in the city is no use to you if the first appointment is in nine weeks.
What the accreditations mean
NABH
National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers

India's national hospital standard. Covers clinical protocols, infection control, staff qualifications, patient rights and medication safety, with periodic reassessment. A hospital without it should not be treating you.

JCI
Joint Commission International

The international benchmark, awarded by a US body and reassessed every three years. Considerably fewer Indian hospitals hold it, which is precisely why it is worth asking about.

Our patients are treated at NABH and JCI accredited hospitals across Delhi and Gurugram, including several of India's largest private hospital groups. We will name the specific hospital we recommend for your case, and explain why, in your written opinion.

Our hospital network

Patients we have helped

We are collecting written permission from former patients to publish their cases in full — condition, hospital, consultant, outcome and what they actually paid. We would rather show you ten real, verifiable stories than fifty invented ones.

Until then, here is what we can offer instead. Ask us, and we will connect you with a former patient from your own country who has agreed to speak with people considering treatment. You can ask them anything you like, and we will not be on the call.

Ask to speak with a former patient

We are a facilitator, not a hospital

TIB HIND does not provide medical treatment, diagnosis or emergency care. All treatment is delivered by independent, accredited hospitals and their consultants, who remain solely responsible for clinical decisions.

Costs are ranges, not quotations

Published figures are indicative ranges based on recent cases. Your final cost is set by the treating hospital after clinical assessment and can change if your treatment does.

Your medical records

Reports you send are reviewed by our medical team and are not shared with any hospital without your instruction. See our privacy and data protection policy.

This site is not for emergencies

If you have chest pain, stroke symptoms, severe bleeding or any acute deterioration, contact your local emergency services now. Do not wait for a reply from us.
